instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Return to the First Hope
cards.instruction: Return to an early hope after every setback, expanding its meaning until the whole scene seems to fulfill it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We wanted a home we could call ours. Start the cottage survey with the roof, please; don't just circle every leak.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole roof needs replacing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then measure it properly. We'll choose every tile together; that makes it ours more thoroughly than a fresh coat of paint.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It could take all our savings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put the money under 'our roof', not 'money gone'. Then let's choose what we can do ourselves. We wanted to belong somewhere; we can start by knowing what holds it up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This concert was meant to bring the village together. Keep everyone facing the stage while I check the sound.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The power's out. No microphones.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then start a song everyone knows, in unison. Please don't have the soloist competing with a silent amplifier.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Half the audience has gone home for torches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the chorus going until they return. Put them round the singers with the lights; don't count those seats as lost audience. They're our lighting crew now.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Warmth with a Countdown
cards.instruction: Perform increasing warmth with increasingly final language, as though every act of care might also be a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my good teacup to your new desk. Wrap the handle separately, please; I want you to have something of our afternoons.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm moving to the desk by the window. It's six feet away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A new beginning deserves proper things. Put this saucer underneath, not against the handle; I won't have your first day spoiled by a breakage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll still see me every morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you'll always be welcome. One final check: cup, saucer, spoon. Take the good spoon too, my dear; don't leave here with anything missing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed sandwiches for your journey. Put the soft ones on top, please; you deserve a proper meal when you arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm only going to the next town. I'll be back by seven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take dinner as well in case seven becomes later. Keep it in the cool bag; I don't want you depending on strangers to feed you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring the bag and containers back tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep them, sweetheart. Please take the lids that fit; I want you properly equipped. No need to bring anything back for my sake.

cards.title: Everything Has Two Prices
cards.instruction: Price every offer twice: once in practical terms and again through an emotional cost that grows when the offer returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll drive you for five pounds' petrol and a conversation about why you stopped calling. Please keep those two parts separate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's ten. Can we leave now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take five back. Extra petrol doesn't answer the question; tell me which evening you decided not to ring.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call tomorrow and explain. Could I still have the lift?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five pounds, and tell me why I should keep tomorrow free after the last three times. Please don't offer another date until you've accounted for the ones I kept.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can borrow my dress for ten pounds and an apology for calling it awful in front of our friends. Money first, then words, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's twenty. I really need it tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take ten. Please don't confuse extra rental with an apology; the dress didn't insult itself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. It's beautiful. Can I wear it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, after you tell those same friends you borrowed it from me. Say you asked, not that I dressed you; I want your choice clear when they see it.

cards.title: Agree to the Exact Words
cards.instruction: Agree to the exact wording, then use later callbacks to narrow what those words can obligate you to do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll carry one box. Mark the chosen one clearly before I lift anything, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said you'd help me move. There's a whole room here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: By carrying one box. Please don't count the room as a container; choose the box covered by the offer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then take the biggest. It's full of books.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tape the base first. I'll carry that one, then I'm finished; helping with the room was the one box, not everything left after it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I agreed to watch your dog today. Please give me a collection time before midnight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow's only a few hours away. I could come at one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One is tomorrow. Put the handover inside today; we need the right date, not the nearest convenient hour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said you loved having him here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I do. His food and lead will be packed for you by eleven. Please collect both with him; loving the guest doesn't change the word 'today'.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You promised the bride we could open the hall without bothering her. Keep its key away from that teacup; the invitation has our only copy of the address.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Too late. The key fell in. I dried it with the invitation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stop rubbing. The paper's stuck to the key and the ink is running; lay them flat before separating them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can peel the paper off, but the address is gone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dry the key on a cloth and call the bride. Ask for the address again; don't lead with 'we've got the key' when we no longer know where to take it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You called the spare chair unnecessary, then put the birthday cake on it. Our birthday guest has the piano stool, and the pianist needs it back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake needs a flat place. I can't put it on someone's lap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then serve the cake and free the chair. Move the guest onto it before asking the pianist to play, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't cut it until he's played Happy Birthday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask the birthday guest to stand while we sing and serve. Pianist on the stool, then song, then cake, then the guest gets the chair. Give them the first slice, please.
